title: Reinstated Installment: Balance and Spread
content:
Patient Financial Services calculation note — **Patient Payment Plans**: the re-enrolled amount, the reinstated balance and the reinstated installment of a defaulted plan put back in force.

## Formal statement

The re-enrolled amount is the amount released back to the invoice when the plan defaulted.

The reinstated balance is the re-enrolled amount plus the plan ledger's own balance, that is the invoice balances enrolled less every payment and every release on the plan ledger, which after a default is the payments posted since the default shown as a negative figure.

The reinstated installment is the reinstated balance divided by the installments still to fall due under the term, rounded to the nearest cent with an exact half cent rounded up, and it is never below the installment the plan carried when it defaulted; when the quotient is lower, the reinstated installment is that installment (a floor of 1 full pre-default installment).

The installments still to fall due under the term are the term's installments less those whose due date has already passed, the passed ones counted as the whole months from the plan's first due date to today plus one, and the reinstated installment applies from the next installment onward.

## Reading the ledger

| Quantity | Read from |
|---|---|
| Amount released at default | The release line on the plan ledger whose reason is the plan's default |
| Invoice balances enrolled | Every enrollment line on the plan ledger, added together |
| Payments | Every payment line on the plan ledger, of every kind, added together |
| Releases | Every release line on the plan ledger, of every reason, added together |
| Installment carried at default | The regular monthly installment on the plan record |
| First due date | The due date of installment 1 on the plan record |

## Worked note (hypothetical 12-month plan)

One invoice enrolled at 1,200.00. Down payment of 120.00 paid at acceptance and three scheduled installments of 90.00 paid (together 390.00). At default, 810.00 was released back to the invoice. Since the default, an arrears payment of 180.00 has been posted. Installment carried at default 90.00. First due date 1 February; today 10 July.

1. Re-enrolled amount: **810.00**.
2. Plan ledger's own balance: 1,200.00 less 570.00 of payments (390.00 and 180.00) less 810.00 of releases, that is **minus 180.00** — the payment since the default, shown as a negative figure.
3. Reinstated balance: 810.00 together with the ledger's negative 180.00, that is 810.00 less 180.00, **630.00**.
4. Installments passed: 5 whole months from 1 February to 10 July, plus one, is 6; still to fall due: 12 less 6, that is **6**.
5. Quotient: 630.00 divided by 6 is 105.00, which is not below 90.00.
6. Reinstated installment: **105.00**, from the next installment onward.

**Floor reached.** Had the reinstated balance been 450.00, the quotient would be 75.00, below the 90.00 carried at default, and the reinstated installment would be 90.00.
